#include <iostream>

using namespace std;

 

struct Node {

    int data;

    Node* prev;

    Node* next;

};

 

// Function to insert at beginning

void insertAtBeginning(Node*& head, int value) {

    Node* newNode = new Node{value, nullptr, head};

 

    if (head != nullptr) {

        head->prev = newNode;

    }

 

    head = newNode;

}

#include <iostream>

using namespace std;

 

struct Node {

    int data;

    Node* prev;

    Node* next;

};

 

// Function to search an element in DLL

int searchElement(Node* head, int key) {

    int position = 1;

    Node* temp = head;

 

    while (temp != nullptr) {

        if (temp->data == key)

            return position;

        temp = temp->next;

        position++;

    }

 

    return -1; // Not found

}

lq.QUESTION_DESC: Consider you are developing a photo album manager application. Each photo in the album is represented as a node in a doubly linked list. The application should support the following features: Add Photo: Insert a new photo into the album at any specific position Remove Photo: Remove a photo from the album by its ID. Move Photo: Move a photo to a different position in the album. Display Album: Display all photos in the album in their current order. How would you implement these functionalities using a Doubly linked list? Each node will represent a photo, and it will have the following fields: photoID: A unique integer identifier for each photo. prev: A pointer to the previous node in the list. next: A pointer to the next node in the list.
